cards.front: Recall a key point about Rights of the UK Citizen
cards.back: The right to a fair trial (Article 6 ECHR) includes the right to a hearing within a reasonable time, an independent tribunal, the presumption of innocence and the right to legal representation

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rights of the UK Citizen
cards.back: In criminal cases, Article 6 guarantees the right to examine witnesses and to have the free assistance of an interpreter if needed

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rights of the UK Citizen
cards.back: The right to jury trial in England and Wales applies to indictable offences tried in the Crown Court, providing lay participation in the justice system

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rights of the UK Citizen
cards.back: Freedom of expression (Article 10 ECHR) protects the right to hold opinions and to receive and impart information and ideas without interference by public authority

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rights of the UK Citizen
cards.back: Freedom of expression is a qualified right: restrictions are permitted if prescribed by law, pursuing a legitimate aim and necessary in a democratic society

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rights of the UK Citizen
cards.back: The right to respect for private and family life (Article 8 ECHR) covers physical and moral integrity, personal autonomy and relationships

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rights of the UK Citizen
cards.back: Article 8 is qualified: interferences can be justified for reasons including national security, public safety, prevention of disorder or crime, and protection of the rights of others

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rights of the UK Citizen
cards.back: Legal aid provides publicly funded legal assistance to those who cannot afford representation, though eligibility has been significantly restricted by the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012 (LASPO)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rights of the UK Citizen
cards.back: The right to vote is a fundamental democratic right; the Representation of the People Act 1983 and subsequent legislation govern who may vote in UK elections

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rights of the UK Citizen
cards.back: Citizens have legal responsibilities including obeying the law, paying taxes, serving on a jury if called and complying with court orders

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rights of the UK Citizen
cards.back: The Rule of Law, as articulated by Dicey, requires that everyone including the government is subject to the same law, that the law is certain and accessible, and that rights are enforced through the courts

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rights of the UK Citizen
cards.back: Balancing rights with responsibilities is fundamental: the exercise of one person's rights must not unduly infringe the rights of others or the interests of society
